problem.title: Is Your Child Prepared for a World That Doesn't Play by the Rules?
problem.subtitle: The world is changing faster than the school system. While other kids are building the future, is yours just consuming it?
problem.card1Text: Imagine your child not just watching videos, but building the next viral app. Every hour spent scrolling is an hour they could spend creating something that matters. The good news? It's not too late to shift from passive consumer to active creator.
problem.card2Text: While schools focus on memorizing facts, successful kids are learning to build, pitch, and sell. Your child has the potential to understand money, create digital products, and think like an entrepreneur. They just need the right environment to unlock it.
problem.card3Text: Every child who launches their first project experiences a transformation. They stand taller. Speak clearer. Believe in themselves. That confidence doesn't come from participation trophies—it comes from building something real and presenting it to the world.
problem.card4Text: Ages 11-14 are the prime years for developing entrepreneurial thinking. Miss this window, and it becomes exponentially harder later. But catch it now, and you're setting your child up with skills that compound for life.
problem.card5Text: Right now, thousands of kids are learning to code, launching businesses, and building portfolios. The gap grows every month. But here's the inspiring part: your child can join them. They can be the one with a real project, real skills, and a real competitive edge.
problem.ctaText: In 9 months, your child will either have a working project they're proud of and skills that set them apart... or they'll still be wondering 'what if?'

program.title: Your Child's 9-Month Journey from Idea to Investor Pitch
program.subtitle: A proven step-by-step system that transforms curious kids into confident young entrepreneurs
program.phase1Items: How businesses actually make money (revenue models, profit & loss) • How to identify a problem worth solving (market research basics) • How to validate an idea before building it (customer interviews, surveys) • The difference between a hobby and a business
program.phase1Outcome: A validated business idea and a one-page business plan that answers: What problem am I solving? Who is my customer? How will I make money?
program.phase1Tools: Miro (brainstorming), Google Slides (presentations), Business Model Canvas
program.phase2Items: UI/UX Design: How to design a product people actually want to use • Prototyping: Turning ideas into clickable mockups • Coding basics: Python or JavaScript (depending on the project) • Project management: Breaking big goals into small tasks
program.phase2Outcome: A working Minimum Viable Product (MVP) — a game, website, or app that actually works and can be tested with real users.
program.phase3Items: Go-to-Market Strategy: How to get your first customers • Digital Marketing: Social media, email, content creation • Sales Funnels: How to turn interest into action • Pitch Deck Creation: Telling your story in 10 slides
program.phase3Outcome: A complete investor pitch deck and a simple marketing plan to launch the product.
program.phase3Tools: Canva (pitch deck design), Google Analytics (tracking), Mailchimp (email marketing)
program.phase4Items: Public Speaking: How to command a room (or a Zoom call) • Storytelling: Turning data into a compelling narrative • Handling Q&A: Answering tough questions with confidence
program.phase4Outcome: A confident, polished pitch presented to a panel of real entrepreneurs for a chance to win $3,000 in seed funding.
program.phase4Tools: Graduation ceremony, certificates, and a portfolio piece your child can use for college applications or future opportunities.
